title: MAFin: Maximizing Accuracy in FinFET based Approximated Real-Time Computing
problem: Maximizing Quality of Service (QoS) in approximate real-time computing systems on FinFET-based multicore platforms while respecting task deadlines and system constraints. Tasks divide into mandatory parts (producing acceptable results) and optional parts (refining accuracy).
motivation: Exploiting unique temperature characteristics of FinFET processors can enhance accuracy and energy efficiency in real-time systems where deadlines are critical.
method: MAFin performs task-to-core allocation and real-time scheduling on FinFET multicores. It exploits the Temperature Effect Inversion (TEI) property where processor speed increases with temperature. During execution, a temperature-cognizant frequency management mechanism dynamically balances performance and temperature, trading off reduced execution time to either execute more optional task parts for higher QoS or power off cores for energy savings.
key_novelty: Leveraging the counterintuitive Temperature Effect Inversion property of FinFET processors, where higher temperature increases speed, to simultaneously maximize QoS and improve energy efficiency in real-time computing.
contributions: MAFin real-time scheduler exploiting FinFET TEI property for QoS maximization
Task-to-core allocation algorithm respecting system-wide constraints
Online temperature-cognizant dynamic frequency management mechanism
Novel exploitation of temperature effects to trade execution time for QoS enhancement or energy efficiency

metrics.accuracy: 70% QoS baseline, 8.3% enhancement with online optimization

primary_theme: Temperature-aware scheduling for FinFET approximate real-time computing
